subject: coding dynamic community model with data in vectorial form

messages.author: 074a030d0cd7e490
messages.subject: coding dynamic community model with data in vectorial form
parts:
Hi everybody, 

I am trying to save time by running an occupancy dynamic community model with data in vectorial form, following page 311 (Chpt 5.4) of AHM2.

With data in a four-dimensional array, my BUGS language observation model would include the command:

 y[i,j,t,k] ~ dbern(z[i,t,k] * pg[i,j,t,k])

Of course this does not work with vectorialized data, because after vectorialization the object 'y' has only two dimensions, with 5 columns that contain numeric information on detection/non-detecion, site, survey, year, and species.

The question is how to direct jags to the correct element of the first column?

If the BUGS language had something like a 'which' command (as R does), I would use something like:

y[which(y[,2]==i & y[,3]==j & y[,4]==t & y[,5]==k),1] ~ dbern(z[i,t,k] * pg[i,j,t,k])

But this did not work, of course.

Does anyone have a solution for this? Thanks for the attention!

Gonçalo

messages.author: 7f4225fd2234920f
messages.subject: Re: coding dynamic community model with data in vectorial form
parts:
Hi Goncalo -

I haven't looked at that section of the AHM2 code, but I think this might work:

For simplicity, I'd separate the various columns of y
ylong = y[,1]
site = y[,2]
survey = y[,3]
year = y[,4]
species = y[,5]

Then you can loop through the elements of ylong (in order) and use the site, survey, year, and species columns as indices to point to the proper element in z or pg that's associated with a particular detection/nondetection observation like:

for(s in 1:length(ylong)) {
ylong[s]  ~ dbern(z[site[s],year[s],species[s]] * pg[site[s],survey[s],year[s],species[s]])
}

You may need to fuss with the site, survey, survey, and year columns to make sure that they can be used as indices and point to the correct element of z and pg, but hopefully this general approach might address your question?

Best,
erin

messages.subject: Re: coding dynamic community model with data in vectorial form
parts:
Dear Goncalo, Erin,

that's great about this list: less than 60 mins you can already get an answer. I think Erin says it right, but I also wanted to point out an example of a model for long-form data in Chapter 4 of the AHM2, for a single-season dynocc model (page 269). The main relevant parts go like this, below. So: no change in the state model: you can define the latent variables in there in their usual arrayed format, which is convenient. Only change really in the observation model.

Best regards  -- Marc

# Ecological submodel: Define state conditional on parameters
for (i in 1:nsites){
  z[i,1] ~ dbern(psi1)
  for (t in 2:nyears){
    z[i,t] ~ dbern(z[i,t-1]*phi[t-1] + (1-z[i,t-1])*gamma[t-1])
  }
}
# Observation model
for (i in 1:nobs){
  logit(p[i]) <- alpha.lp[year[i]] + beta.lp.1[year[i]] * date[i] +
    beta.lp.2[year[i]] * pow(date[i],2) + eps.site[site[i], year[i]]
  y[i] ~ dbin(z[site[i],year[i]]*p[i], nsurveys[i])
}

Dear Erin (and Marc)
Thank you for your quick reply, which makes a lot of sense and works too. It took me and Fábio (cc) one week to implement because other things got in the way, but it solved the problem very well. We ended up calling for the different columns of y within the ‘dbern’ command without actually splitting y into different objects, but the idea is the same. I can see it in Marc’s code below, as well.
This list is great. I really appreciate your help!
Gonçalo
